theater: 耶路撒冷城垣與猶大王國南部邊境

battle.name: 猶大-巴比倫戰爭
battle.theater: 耶路撒冷城垣與猶大王國南部邊境
battle.brief: 前601年，新巴比倫王尼布甲尼撒二世把軍隊推過亞拉巴曠野，戰線直抵猶大與埃及的交界，這場戰爭自此拖成前597年與前587/586年兩次圍困耶路撒冷。卡面的埃及長矛正是埃及援軍步兵的制式武器，猶大守軍的鄉土步兵也用同一款式，而真正決定勝負的其實是糧道與城門。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 新巴比倫帝國與猶大王國是這場戰爭的兩方，埃及薩伊王朝則以援軍與物資介入，構成三方糾纏。巴比倫一方是高度中央集權的國家：國王尼布甲尼撒二世直轄一支「王軍」，骨幹是來自北部比爾森河流域的迦勒底（Kaldu）部族步兵與弓兵，配以雙輪戰車隊、輕騎、工兵與攻城技師；王宮大門浮雕上的「蠍子」近衛象徵王軍的精銳部分。外圍是各行省守軍、徵召民兵與附屬國貢軍。命令透過王室書記官發出的文書與信差下達，稅收與徵發由「河外省」總督及各城書記經手，後勤依托幼發拉底河的水路、皇家大道與沿途的關卡驛站。猶大一方是前586年仍殘存的小型附庸王國：軍隊以步兵與弓兵為主，車兵到六世紀末已近乎廢止，城防依靠城牆、角樓與聖殿區高台；王室的權力與聖殿的財政捆綁在一起，王宮同時是兵員與錢糧的來源。埃及的介入出自區域格局：前589年出兵是想把巴比倫的西界推回幼發拉底河，並保住通往敘利亞與腓尼基的商路。對三方而言，這一條走廊的歸屬才是戰爭的真正賭注。
countriesEn: The two belligerents in this war were the Neo-Babylonian Empire and the Kingdom of Judah, with the Saite dynasty of Egypt entering the conflict with troops and supplies, which made it a three-cornered struggle. On the Babylonian side the state was highly centralised: King Nebuchadnezzar II commanded a royal army whose core was infantry and archers drawn from the Chaldean, or Kaldu, tribal contingents of northern Babylonia, backed by war chariots, light cavalry, engineers and siege craftsmen; the Scorpion guard shown on the palace gate reliefs symbolised the elite of this royal force. Around it stood provincial garrisons, conscript levies and contingents supplied by vassal states. Orders travelled by documents and couriers issued from the king's scribes; taxation and requisition were handled by the governor of the province Beyond the River together with city scribes, and logistics rode on Euphrates shipping, the royal road and the customs stations along it. Judah on the other side was a small client kingdom still surviving in 586 BC: its army was infantry and archers, the chariot corps having almost died out by the end of the sixth century, and its defence rested on city walls, corner towers and the high ground of the Temple Mount; the power of the palace was welded to the finances of the Temple, and the royal household doubled as the source of soldiers and grain. Egypt's involvement came out of the regional balance of power: the expedition of 589 BC was meant to push the Babylonian frontier back to the Euphrates and to keep the trade roads through Syria and Phoenicia open. For all three parties, control of that corridor was the real stake of the war.
people: 核心人物是尼布甲尼撒二世（前626至前562年在位，前605年正式即位）。他先在卡爾凱美什打敗埃及法老尼可二世（前610至前595年在位），奪得黎凡特；前601年他把兵鋒推過阿拉伯曠野，在泰馬留下石碑；前597年第一次圍困耶路撒冷；前587/586年再發大軍攻取該城，隨後重建巴比倫的伊什塔拉門與埃薩吉拉神廟。他的父親那波帕拉沙爾與米底王基阿克薩雷斯結盟，前612年攻下尼尼微、前609年取哈倫，滅掉亞述，為兒子騰出西界。猶大方面：前609年在美吉多陣亡的約西亞留下王位；其子西雅敬在巴比倫第一次圍城期間（前605/604年）死於耶路撒冷；西雅敬之子約雅斤前597年即位、隨即被廢，囚於巴比倫直至去世；其弟西底家是巴比倫扶立的傀儡，前589年公開倒向埃及，前586年城破被擄。《耶利米書》二十二章把這位被廢國王判為不生育，連血脈都被否認；西底家身邊有先知耶利米在城內周旋，被擄之後又被帶往埃及；第一批被擄的官員在巴比倫留下了《以西結書》，以寄居者的角度記錄同一場災難。埃及方面，除前589年出兵的王（學界或指普桑提克三世，或據《耶利米書》指合法拉）外，還有前586年率數百名猶大軍人逃往埃及的兵長耶胡卡爾，他的名字出現在塔赫帕內斯的韋茨曼紙草文書裡。巴比倫方面的執行者還包括事後被任為省長的基大利，以及以他媽押為首、十人參與的武裝刺殺團，他們在前582年於米茲帕殺了基大利，卻沒有能力重建王國。
peopleEn: The central figure is Nebuchadnezzar II, on the throne from 626 to 562 BC and crowned king in 605 BC. He first broke Pharaoh Necho II, who ruled from 610 to 595 BC, at Carchemish and took the Levant; in 601 BC he drove his army across the Arabian desert and left a stele at Tema; in 597 BC he besieged Jerusalem for the first time; in 587/586 BC he came back with a great army, took the city, and then rebuilt the Ishtar Gate and the Esagila temple in Babylon. His father Nabopolassar had allied with the Median king Cyaxares, taking Nineveh in 612 BC and Harran in 609 BC, and so cleared the western horizon for his son. On the Judean side, Josiah, who fell at Megiddo in 609 BC, left the throne behind; his son Jehoiakim died inside Jerusalem during the first Babylonian siege of 605/604 BC; Jehoiachin, who took the throne in 597 BC, was deposed at once and kept in Babylon until his death; his brother Zedekiah, a puppet installed by Babylon, threw in his lot with Egypt in 589 BC and was taken captive when the city fell in 586 BC. Jeremiah 22 judges the deposed king childless and so denies even his line; around Zedekiah worked the prophet Jeremiah, who moved inside the city, was imprisoned, and after the surrender was carried off to Egypt; the officials deported in the first wave left the book of Ezekiel in Babylon, recording the same disaster from the point of view of the exiles. On the Egyptian side there was the king who sent the army of 589 BC, identified by scholars either as Psamtik III or, following Jeremiah, as Hophra, and there was the Judean commander Yehucal, who led several hundred of his men into Egypt in 586 BC and whose name appears in the Weizmann papyrus from Tahpanhes. On the Babylonian side the executors of the settlement included Gedaliah, appointed governor, and the armed band of ten men under Ishmael ben Nethaniah, who killed Gedaliah at Mizpah in 582 BC without any capacity to restore the kingdom.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬於青銅時代以來的路標兵器：狹長的銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆前端，杆長約兩米，雙手持握，刺擊為主、劈砍為輔，正好配合密集縱隊的用法。晚古埃及的薩伊時期仍是埃及步兵的制式長矛，猶大與黎凡特各城邦自中青銅時代起也沿用同一款式，兩地在武器上並無明顯隔閡，所以這件兵器在戰役裡的定位很清楚：它是埃及援軍步兵的標準刺擊武器，同時也是猶大守軍鄉土步兵的主要兵器，而巴比倫人的長矛式樣更接近亞述系的寬刃型。戰役中實際出現的其他兵器包括埃及與黎凡特通用的複合弓與銅箭鏈，以及薩伊時期大量僱用的希臘與卡里亞弓手；埃及鐮刀式短劍，即比梅勒碑上的國王手中所持的那一類，與其後被繼承的亞述式直刃短劍；猶大守軍的短投槍；攻城用的鐵頭撞槌、木架攻城塔、築在城牆外的土石斜坡、工兵的鎬與繩鉤，以及用來護住撞槌操作組的成排木盾與蒙皮帳板。運輸與後勤工具包括牛拉的四輪車、帳篷車、驢隊、駱駝隊，以及沿幼發拉底河與海口轉運的船隻。埃及人還有一支帶木製荊棘馬刺的騎兵，用來對付密集步兵，據希羅多德記載這支部隊在薩伊王朝已存在。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a landmark of the Bronze Age: a narrow copper or bronze blade lashed to the front of a wooden shaft about two metres long, gripped in both hands, made for thrusting rather than cutting, and therefore exactly suited to the tight files of a phalanx-like formation. In the late Saite period it was still the standard spear of Egyptian infantry, and Judah and the Levantine city states had used the same pattern since the Middle Bronze Age, so there was no real divide between the two sides over this arm: it is the standard thrusting weapon of the Egyptian relief infantry and at the same time the principal arm of the Judean levy, while the Babylonian spear was of the broader Assyrian type. The actual weapons present in the campaign included composite bows with copper arrowheads, shared by Egypt and the Levant, together with the large numbers of Greek and Carian archers the Saite kings hired; the Egyptian sickle sword, the type of weapon the king on the Bimele stele is shown holding, and the Assyrian-style straight blade that succeeded it; the short javelins of the Judean garrison; and the siege train: iron-headed battering rams, wooden siege towers, earthen and stone ramps built against the walls, the picks and grappling hooks of the engineers, and the rows of wooden and hide-covered screens that protected the ram crews. Transport and supply came on ox-drawn four-wheeled carts, covered wagons, mule trains, camel trains, and by barge and ship along the Euphrates and the coast. The Egyptians also fielded cavalry armed with wooden caltrops to break massed infantry, a unit already in existence under the Saite kings according to Herodotus.
tactics: 巴比倫的攻城辦法在亞述時代已定型，前597與前586兩次圍城都沿用同一套流程：先以弓兵與投石手壓制城頭，輪流替換不讓守軍喘息；再以工兵在城牆外築斜坡，用壘石與土方把高度墊到與城頭相當，斜坡兩側設有護廊，撞槌隊沿坡道把人頭撞向門樓與城牆根部，工兵則同時在牆基掏挖坑道；攻城塔在後方推進，塔上射手與隨塔步兵掩護撞槌；最後在城門與城牆的薄弱處同時實施破壞，缺口一開，守軍的縱列便被湧入的隊伍切斷。拉基什浮雕把這套流程畫得極細，包括投石手的拋擲姿勢、梯架與斜坡的接駁，以及工兵在護廊下的作業方式。守城一方則倚賴地形：耶路撒冷坐落在山脊分水嶺上，東西兩側是陡坡，東面有以賽亞時期開鑿的西羅亞運渠供水，北面居高臨下，防守重點集中在北門與城牆轉角，聖殿區的高台同時是預備隊與指揮部所在。糧食是守軍真正的弱點：巴比倫封鎖城郊道路與水源，徵收鄉村存糧，最後是靠城外逐點掃清與飢餓逼出內部的投降與開城。埃及的救援想用沿海的補給線換取時間：先解加薩之圍再北上，但步兵一旦離開尼羅河三角洲的水網進入開闊平原，就在巴比倫的弓騎面前失去縱隊優勢，救援最終退回埃及。巴比倫自己也避免在冬季、以及在耶路撒冷南面起伏的山脊地作戰，進攻多安排在春末夏初。
tacticsEn: The Babylonian method of siege had been fixed since the Assyrian age, and both the siege of 597 and that of 586 BC followed the same sequence: archers and slingers first suppressed the wall so that the defenders could not answer, with crews rotated so that the defenders never got a respite; engineers then built a ramp outside the wall, packing stone and earth to raise it level with the parapet, with covered galleries along its sides, the ram crews pushing up the ramp to strike the gate towers and the foot of the wall, while miners opened galleries under the base; siege towers advanced behind, their archers and their escorting infantry covering the ram; and finally the gate and the weakest stretch of the curtain were broken at the same moment, and once the breach opened the defenders' files were cut apart by the troops pouring through. The Lachish relief shows the whole procedure in detail, including the throwing posture of the slingers, the join between tower and ramp, and the engineers working under the gallery. The defenders relied on the terrain: Jerusalem stands on a watershed ridge with steep slopes to east and west, fed by the Siloam channel cut under Hezekiah, commanding the approach from the north, with the main defence concentrated on the northern gate and the corner of the wall, and the high platform of the Temple Mount serving at once as the reserve and as the command post. Grain was the garrison's real weakness: Babylon sealed the roads and the water sources around the city and levied the stores of the countryside, and it was famine and the failure of morale that finally produced surrender and a gate opened from within. Egypt's relief force hoped to buy time with a supply line along the coast, relieving Gaza before moving north, but once the infantry left the water network of the Nile delta and came out onto the open plain, they lost the advantage of formation against Babylonian mounted archers, and the expedition withdrew to Egypt. The Babylonians in turn avoided campaigning in winter and on the ridges south of Jerusalem, preferring to attack in late spring and early summer.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下：戰爭的前601年是開端，前597年是第一次圍城，前587/586年是第二次圍城與聖殿的毀滅，中間相隔近十年。巴比倫遠征軍的規模以「國王大軍」計，兵種含步兵、弓兵、騎兵、雙輪戰車與隨軍工匠，總量在數萬之數，但沒有留下可核的編制表。猶大守軍的人數不詳，只能從《列王紀下》第二十四章被擄名單反推：王室成員與官員、七千名軍官、一千名工匠與二百名鐵匠，連同家眷合計約上萬人。耶路撒冷城牆的考古測量約厚三至四公尺，最高處約十公尺，聖殿區的圍牆更高。聖殿被運走的器物有兩根銅柱、銅海、金碗、燈臺、陳設餅桌與金號，加上「其餘的戰車」。埃及援軍的兵力沒有留下記錄，但其存在由《耶利米書》第四十四章提到的埃及諸首領，以及在塔赫帕內斯定居的猶大移民互相印證。傳統把聖殿毀滅記在猶太曆阿布月九日，相當於巴比倫曆塔穆茲第四月，與編年史把攻陷耶路撒冷記在尼布甲尼撒二世第十八年互相吻合。還有一方新巴比倫王宮泥板記下「猶大國王在巴比倫逝世」一條，一般考訂為被囚多年的約雅斤，也有學者認為指的是西底家。距離方面，巴比倫到耶路撒冷直線約一千二百公里，軍隊實際沿幼發拉底河與商路分段推進。
dataEn: The verifiable figures run roughly as follows. The war opens in 601 BC; the first siege falls in 597 BC; the second siege and the destruction of the Temple come in 587/586 BC, with almost ten years between them. The size of the Babylonian expedition is given only as the king's great army, combining infantry, archers, cavalry, war chariots and attached engineers, and it is generally reckoned in the tens of thousands, but no muster survives. The strength of the Judean garrison is unknown and can only be inferred from the list of exiles in the twenty-fourth chapter of 2 Kings: the royal household and officials, seven thousand soldiers, a thousand craftsmen and two hundred smiths, with their households making something in the order of ten thousand people in all. Archaeological measurement of Jerusalem's First Wall gives a thickness of roughly three to four metres and a height of up to about ten metres, with the Temple Mount enclosure higher still. The Temple plate that was carried off comprised the two bronze pillars, the bronze sea, the golden bowls, the lampstand, the table of showbread and the golden trumpets, together with the rest of the chariots. No figure survives for the Egyptian expedition, but its presence is confirmed by the princes of Egypt named in the forty-fourth chapter of Jeremiah and by the Judean settlement at Tahpanhes. Tradition dates the destruction of the Temple to the ninth of the Jewish month of Av, which corresponds to the fourth Babylonian month of Tammuz, and this agrees with the chronicle's placing of the capture of Jerusalem in Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth regnal year. A clay tablet from the Neo-Babylonian palace records the death of a king of Judah in Babylon, generally identified with Jehoiachin, though some scholars read it as Zedekiah. As for distance, Babylon lies roughly twelve hundred kilometres from Jerusalem in a straight line, and the army worked its way forward in stages along the Euphrates and the caravan roads.
cause: 起因是多層的。遠因是前612年亞述覆亡留下的權力真空：幼發拉底河中游的新巴比倫、尼亞河谷的米底、埃及三角洲，三方都想填上這個空缺，而敘利亞與黎凡特海岸是爭奪的重心。前605年巴比倫在卡爾凱美什擊敗尼可二世，埃及退出黎凡特，但到前601年這個格局仍未穩定，巴比倫還得先把西南翼的阿拉伯邊境與埃及的影響清乾淨，泰馬石碑就是這一步的見證。直接原因則在猶大這一邊：西雅敬與約雅斤兩朝長期只在名義上臣服，交納的貢賦又遠低於巴比倫要求的數目，前597年約雅斤抗命、拒絕接待巴比倫派來的使臣，成為導火線。更深一層，是朝貢體系本身不容許一個小國長期含糊其辭：巴比倫需要的不是一個朋友，而是一個能提供稅源、通道與穩定邊界的行省。猶大想要耶路撒冷的都城地位與聖殿的自主，巴比倫要的則是一條從幼發拉底河到地中海的完整控制線，兩者的要求本來就無法同時成立。加上前589年耶路撒冷得到埃及的公開支援，任何收束都要先解決埃及的介入，戰爭因此拖成兩輪。
causeEn: The causes worked on several levels. In the background lay the power vacuum left by the fall of Assyria in 612 BC: the new Babylon on the middle Euphrates, the Medes in the Ninear valley and Egypt in the delta all wanted to fill it, and Syria and the Levantine coast were the prize. After Babylon beat Necho II at Carchemish in 605 BC, Egypt withdrew from the Levant, but by 601 BC the new order was not settled, and the south-western flank still had to be cleared of the Arabian frontier and of Egyptian influence, which is exactly what the Tema stele witnesses. The immediate cause lay on the Judean side: the reigns of Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin acknowledged Babylonian overlordship only in name and paid in tribute far less than was demanded, and in 597 BC the refusal of Jehoiachin to admit the Babylonian emissaries became the trigger. Deeper still was the tribute system itself, which could not tolerate a small state long remaining ambiguous: Babylon did not want a friend but a province able to yield taxes, a corridor and a settled frontier. Judah wanted the standing of a capital with an autonomous Temple; Babylon wanted an unbroken line of control from the Euphrates to the Mediterranean, and the two demands were never compatible. Add the open Egyptian support that came to Jerusalem in 589 BC, and any settlement had to dispose of the Egyptian intervention first, which is why the war came in two rounds.
impact: 最深遠的影響是猶大王國的解體。前586年之後，耶路撒冷成了一片廢墟，聖殿被焚，國王的血脈與國家機構被連根拔起；剩下的百姓被併入巴比倫新設的「河外省」，前539年居魯士進巴比倫時又把猶大列為歸附的附庸之一，前538/537年首批被擄者返國，在廢址上重新立起祭壇，前515/516年第二聖殿落成。猶大於是從一個王國轉成散居的教社群體，經卷傳統正是在這段寄居歲月裡整理成形的，例如西番雅在巴比倫所寫的書就是寄居者的文獻。對巴比倫來說，這場戰爭的收穫是西界：從此亞述舊疆的敘利亞到腓尼基都在新王朝的控制之下，首都完成伊什塔拉門與埃薩吉拉的重建，巴比倫的楔形文字行政自前605年起取代亞述的亞蘭語書寫，成為東地中海與伊朗高原之間通用的外交與商業文字，被擄的猶大官員與匠人也把黎凡特的技術與書寫帶進美索不達米亞。就武器而言，前586年之後耶路撒冷再沒有足以容納大型車兵的塹壕與馬道，戰車作為王權象徵的時期在猶大就此結束；前539年後修復的城牆與後來的第二聖殿院落，把城防重新定位在石砌的高牆與狹窄的門樓上，而這正是六百年後起義者仍要面對的地理前提。
impactEn: The deepest effect was the dissolution of the Kingdom of Judah. After 586 BC Jerusalem lay in ruins, the Temple had burned, the royal bloodline and the state apparatus had been torn out by the roots; the remnant population was folded into the new Babylonian province Beyond the River, and when Cyrus entered Babylon in 539 BC Judah was among the peoples listed as submitting. In 538/537 BC the first returning exiles raised the altar again on the ruined site, and the Second Temple was dedicated in 515/516 BC. Judah was thus transformed from a kingdom into a dispersed religious community, and it was in the years of exile that the scriptural tradition was put into order, the book of Zephaniah written in Babylon being the literature of the deportees. For Babylon the prize was the western frontier. From then on Syria and Phoenicia lay under the new dynasty, the capital was rebuilt with the Ishtar Gate and the Esagila, and Babylonian cuneiform administration replaced Assyrian Aramaic writing from 605 BC onward to become the common diplomatic and commercial script between the eastern Mediterranean and the Iranian plateau; the deported Judean officials and craftsmen carried Levantine techniques and texts into Mesopotamia. In military terms, after 586 BC Jerusalem had no ditch and no causeway that could hold a large chariot corps, and the chariot as an image of kingship ended in Judah. The wall rebuilt after 539 BC and the precincts of the later Second Temple redefined the city's defence around high stone curtain walls and narrow gatehouses, and that is precisely the geographical premise the insurgents would confront six centuries later.
result: 結果是巴比倫完勝，而猶大王國不再存在。前597年那一輪，巴比倫其實只用了一場圍城加一次政治處置：攻下耶路撒冷、廢黜約雅斤、擄走王族、官員、匠人與聖殿金器，卻保留城牆與聖殿，讓被擄者安居巴比倫——這是一種示範式的懲罰，目標是讓猶大放棄復國的念頭。前586年那一輪則不同：西底家在得到埃及的公開支援、重整軍備與城防之後，抵抗拖到糧盡與人心潰散，最後以城門被開、突入金殿收場，聖殿與王宮被焚，僅少數人被留作行政人員，基大利被派來治理殘餘百姓，前582年又被以他媽押為首的武裝刺殺。戰役在戰術層面的結論也很清楚：決定勝負的從來不是撞槌與斜坡，而是後勤——巴比倫封住糧道，把戰爭拖成圍城，守軍的壯丁在缺糧中消耗，等到能開城的人出現，攻城技術只是最後一步。對猶大而言，這場戰爭終結了舊王國，並開啟了被擄、寄居、歸回三段式的一千年；對巴比倫而言，它把帝國的西界推到了地中海，也把巴比倫從一個兩河強國變成西亞強權——而這份版圖，最後成為波斯人第一個覬覦的目標。
resultEn: The result was a complete Babylonian victory and the end of the Kingdom of Judah. The round of 597 BC cost Babylon one siege and one political manoeuvre: take Jerusalem, depose Jehoiachin, carry off the royal family, the officials, the craftsmen and the Temple gold, but leave the walls and the sanctuary standing and settle the exiles comfortably in Babylon, an exemplary punishment intended to kill any thought of restoration. The round of 586 BC was different. Zedekiah, having openly taken Egypt's side, rebuilt his army and his defences, held out until hunger and collapsing morale opened the gates, and the assault ended with the palace taken, the Temple and the royal quarter burned, only a handful of people left behind to staff the administration, and Gedaliah appointed over the remnant, only to be killed in 582 BC by an armed band under Ishmael ben Nethaniah. The tactical lesson of the campaign is equally clear: what decided it was never the ram or the ramp but logistics. Babylon closed the grain roads and turned the war into a siege, the garrison's fighting men were consumed by shortage, and once a man inside was willing to open the gate, the siegecraft was only the last step. For Judah the war ended the old kingdom and opened the thousand years of exile, sojourn and return; for Babylon it carried the empire's western frontier to the Mediterranean and turned Babylon from a river power into a western Asian great power, and that territory would be the first thing the Persians came for.
